Senses.Explanation: In Chan records the fly-whisk is the master's teaching-seat implement and an emblem of authority, not merely a duster. Asked what he uses to show people, Baizhang raises the whisk. A master may answer the question of the patriarch's coming from the West by showing it, draw a stroke with it to cut off preceding entanglements, strike the Chan seat or a monk with it, mime playing a flute with it, or throw it down before stepping from the seat. In one encounter a master strikes the visitor across the mouth with the whisk; the visitor seizes it and bows. Another passage explicitly contrasts the two implements: “the staff establishes; the fly-whisk sweeps away,” while calling them equal in weight. Its institutional force is also explicit when a master says that he has tested a disciple and “specially bestows one fly-whisk” so the disciple may continue Dahui's line; another recipient accepts the whisk and states how he will raise it. To brush or whisk away (拂), plus a noun suffix (子): a fly-whisk. The headword occurs 11,115 times in 378 allowlisted texts. A fixed naming test says, “call it a whisk and you offend; do not call it a whisk and you turn your back on it.” An impossible-object form, “tortoise-hair whisk,” is paired with “rabbit-horn staff.” Raising, striking, seizing, drawing, miming, showing, and transmitting all involve the same physical implement; its Zen bend lies in who wields, contests, or bestows it and where it acts.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide object sense: the fly-whisk as teaching-seat implement and emblem of authority. The curated passages include bestowal and receipt as a lineage credential, a nonverbal interview answer, direct striking and seizure, the text's staff/whisk functional contrast, drawing, and representational mime as well as raising, throwing, naming, the impossible variant, the whisk-tip, and striking the seat. These deployments do not create separate object senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問百丈汝以何法示人百丈豎起拂子師云只遮箇為當別有百丈拋下拂子
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Transmission Lamp Jade-Flower Collection (傳燈玉英集), section on Huangbo Xiyun of Hongzhou (洪州黃蘗希運禪師). Huangbo asks Baizhang Huaihai what he uses to show people; Baizhang raises the whisk (豎起拂子) and then throws it down (拋下拂子). This is a narrated two-speaker case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 握拂子云：『喚作拂子則觸，不喚作拂子則背，不得拈起、不得放下、不得下語、不得無語
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A first-person recollection (本師…握拂子云…, "my teacher… gripped the whisk and said…"). The whisk-naming test: gripping the whisk, "call it a whisk and you offend; don't call it a whisk and you turn your back on it" (喚作拂子則觸，不喚作拂子則背), forbidding picking it up (拈起), putting it down (放下), saying a word (下語), and staying wordless (無語). Narrated → MasterName null. Formula attested 31× across 26 texts (e.g. J10nA158, J26nB185).

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「大德龜毛拂子、兔角柱杖藏著何處？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The impossible-object variant 'tortoise-hair whisk' (龜毛拂子) is paired with 'rabbit-horn staff' (兔角拄杖). The occurrence is in dialogue, and the section master for this line is not confirmed, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂舉拂子云大眾從上許多賢聖如今緫在山僧拂子頭上各各坐大蓮華
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄). In a hall act, the master lifts the whisk and says that all the sages from of old are on this mountain monk's whisk-tip (拂子頭).

Occurrences.Kwic: 以拂子擊禪床云當機覿面提覿面當機疾
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄). The stage direction says that the master strikes the Chan seat with the whisk (拂子擊禪床), a recurrent hall gesture.

Occurrences.Kwic: 老僧勘驗有在，特付拂子一枝，以續大慧之裔云。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The speaker says that he has tested the disciple and specially bestows one fly-whisk so that the disciple may continue Dahui's line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲接拂子曰：「直向佛祖斫額不及處提時，當報不報之恩。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The recipient Yun accepts the fly-whisk and states how he will raise it, displaying the receiving side of the authorization event.

Occurrences.Kwic: 以拂子畫一畫，曰：前來葛藤，一時劃斷。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The master draws one stroke with the fly-whisk and says that the preceding entanglements are cut off at once.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問。三乘十二分教則不問。如何是祖師西來的的意。師舉拂子示之。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Asked for the exact meaning of the patriarch's coming from the West, the master raises and shows the fly-whisk as the interview answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 以拂子作品笛勢云：「咿唔。」遂下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In a hall address the master uses the fly-whisk to mime playing a flute, vocalizes, and steps down.

Occurrences.Kwic: 覺以拂子驀口打。師擬開口。覺又打。師於是有省。遂奪拂子。便禮拜。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In a narrated encounter, Zhaojue strikes the visitor across the mouth twice with the fly-whisk; the visitor has an insight, seizes the whisk, and bows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 拄杖建立，拂子掃蕩；一箇半斤，一箇八兩，各顯法門廣博
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The record explicitly contrasts the implements' deployments: the staff establishes and the fly-whisk sweeps away, while calling them equal in weight.
